goal:
T33 — issue each proof certificate once, store it, and let anyone fetch it by id (closes the T32 gap).

Today _mint_proof(evidence_id) creates a new certificate (new certificate_id, issued_at, signature) on every call, so the
signature quoted in a PR body (T32) can never be fetched again and checked. A reviewer must be able to take the
certificate id from the PR, fetch the certificate, and verify it offline with GET /v1/proof/key.

1. services/api/main.py: _mint_proof(evidence_id) returns the stored certificate when one was already issued for that
   evidence; otherwise it mints, stores and returns it. Store certificates durably in the existing evidence store
   (_evidence = postgres_state.ScopedRecords("records")) so it works in memory and PostgreSQL modes — e.g. a record with
   a dedicated id that maps evidence -> certificate and certificate_id -> certificate. Store exactly the signed body
   (never re-sign on read). The HTTP response keeps adding the "verify" envelope field on top.
2. NEW GET /v1/proof/cert/{certificate_id} -> the stored certificate plus "verify"; 404 when unknown.
3. _pr_core quotes the stored certificate (same certificate_id and signature as GET /v1/proof/{evidence_id}).
4. apps/web/lib/proxyPolicy.ts and proxyPolicy.cases.json: allow GET /v1/proof/cert/<id> (same id rules as other id
   routes) with allow and deny cases.
5. Tests: services/api/tests/test_muse_t33.py. Keep all existing tests green.
